name: Vilsalpsee
kurzbeschreibung: The picturesque Vilsalpsee in the Tannheimer Tal captivates with its emerald-green waters and stunning alpine scenery, perfect for hiking and lingering.
preis: Kostenlos (Alpen-Express Bummelzug ca. 5 €, Parkplatz Tannheim ca. 5–7 € pro Tag)
beschreibung:
Overview

Lake Vilsalpsee rests as a deeply cobalt, crystal-clear alpine jewel at an elevation of 1,165 meters in a secluded valley basin branching south from the Tannheimer Tal. Covering approximately 57 hectares with a depth reaching 47 meters, it forms the pristine core of the 18-square-kilometer Vilsalpsee Nature Reserve—one of the oldest and most strictly protected alpine sanctuaries in Tyrol. Guarded by the sheer limestone escarpments of Mount Gaishorn (2,247 m), the Rauhhorn, and the Rote Flüh, the lake provides an oasis of untamed tranquility and rich biological diversity: over 700 flowering plant species thrive here alongside rare alpine waterfowl, such as the great crested grebe. At the far southern head of the lake, the thundering Berggaishorn waterfall cascades over sheer rock amphitheaters, feeding the lake with glacial spring water.

Route & Requirements

Trail options around Vilsalpsee cater to leisure strollers, families, and high-altitude alpine trekkers. The signature outing is the level shoreline circuit: extending roughly 4.2 kilometers, a broad, well-graded gravel promenade hugs the quiet eastern and western banks, leading directly to the historic Vilsalpe alpine dairy (1,175 m) and the foot of the Berggaishorn cataract (walking time approx. 1.5 hours, easy grade T1, fully stroller accessible). For serious mountaineers, Vilsalpsee serves as the primary gateway to the high-alpine domain: past the Vilsalpe, a secured mountain singletrack ascends rocky switchbacks past Lake Traualpsee up to the Landsberger Hütte refuge (1,810 m; 2 to 2.5 hours climb, 650 vertical meters, moderate grade T2, requiring surefootedness on damp rock steps). Walking shoes suffice for the lake promenade; rigid mountaineering boots are mandatory for hut approaches. Leashed dogs are permitted on all reserve trails.

Visit & Arrival

Rail travelers arrive at Reutte in Tirol station or Sonthofen station in Bavaria, connecting to regional VVT bus line 120 heading to Tannheim (Kreisverkehr stop). To safeguard fragile nature reserve ecosystems, the private road between Tannheim and Lake Vilsalpsee is strictly closed to motor vehicles between 10:00 AM and 5:00 PM. During peak hours, the charming "Tannheimer Alpen-Express" motorized road train, horse-drawn carriages, and regular local shuttles ferry visitors from Tannheim's central car park to the lake (15 min). Walkers can stroll the pleasant meadows from Tannheim in about 45 minutes.

Tips

Rent a traditional timber rowboat at the Fischerstube lakeside pier to glide across glassy water toward the roaring southern cascades. Take a well-deserved rest at the rustic Vilsalpe chalet, savoring thick slices of local alpine mountain cheese and fresh buttermilk beneath the towering ramparts of Mount Gaishorn.
saison: Mai bis Oktober (während der Wintermonate Zufahrt teilweise eingeschränkt)
